title: SHIFT(hold) + NUMBER not working to switch between Fancy zones personal layouts

judgment.rationale: The regression is localized to the drag-time FancyZones keyboard condition and has a safe state boundary.
evidence: The report says Shift+number and secondary-button-then-number stopped changing layouts in version 0.101.2362.
Related Issue 21277 documents drag-time quick layout switching as existing behavior.
Current FancyZones code requires Win+Ctrl+Alt+digit for the drag-time path; blame points to PR 48569.
judgment.recommended_action: Approve the fork design for implementation.

fix_assessment.rationale: No existing fix attempt covers the over-restrictive active-drag condition.

proposed_fixes.title: Restore safe quick-layout switching during an active FancyZones drag
proposed_fixes.root_cause: PR 48569 changed the drag-time digit condition to require Win+Ctrl+Alt, so the historical Shift+number and secondary-button drag paths fall through.
plan: In FancyZones::OnKeyDown, distinguish a live move-size session from stale DraggingState by requiring both IsDragging and a non-null active WindowMouseSnap.
Accept digit and numpad digit during that live session while retaining Win+Ctrl+Alt+digit outside a drag.
Add regressions for Shift and secondary-button switching plus the stale-drag number-key safety case.
verification: During a window drag, Shift+2 changes to layout 2 and a secondary-button drag followed by 1 changes to layout 1.
After a window is destroyed mid-drag, digits typed in another application are not consumed by FancyZones.

confidence.rationale: The issue behavior, related historical behavior, current condition, and regression commit align directly.

issue_context.summary: A FancyZones regression removed the simple drag-time layout shortcuts that let users switch personal layouts while positioning a window.
known_information: The reporter can still switch layouts with Win+Alt+Ctrl+number, but that is not usable during the reported drag flow.
Related Issue 21277 establishes that drag-time quick switching was previously supported.
inferences: The regression is more likely an over-broad keyboard guard than a failure to recognize the configured layouts.
The live WindowMouseSnap object is a safer activity signal than DraggingState alone.
issue_context.analysis: The current code path still handles digit selection, but its drag branch now requires three modifiers. Restricting bare digits to a live snapper preserves the stale-state protection that motivated the regression change while restoring the documented interaction.
initial_investigation: Local source inspection identified FancyZones::OnKeyDown, MoveSizeStart/End, and DraggingState as the control flow.
Git blame tied the changed condition to commit dd26d86580 / PR 48569.
Fork mirror Issue 633 contains the detailed design and adversary approval.

design.root_cause: FancyZones::OnKeyDown treats drag-time quick-layout switching as valid only when Win, Ctrl, and Alt are pressed. That condition was introduced to prevent stale drag state from stealing number keys, but it also rejects the active-drag Shift+number and secondary-button+number behaviors.
evidence: [Observed] The reporter reproduces the regression only after version 0.101.2362.
[Observed] Related Issue 21277 records the prior drag-time behavior.
[Observed] Current source has the restrictive modifier condition; git blame identifies PR 48569.
[Inferred] A non-null WindowMouseSnap during move-size is the appropriate additional liveness guard.

affected_files.purpose: Handles keyboard input and move-size lifecycle.
Tracks whether a drag interaction is active.
Provides drag and layout-switching regression coverage.

implementation_steps.current_behavior: The drag branch requires Win+Ctrl+Alt+digit, so Shift+digit and secondary-button+digit are ignored.
implementation_steps.change: Allow a digit only when DraggingState reports a drag and the active WindowMouseSnap exists; keep the modifier-heavy path for non-drag input.
implementation_steps.code_block: bool activeDrag = m_draggingState.IsDragging() && m_windowMouseSnapper != nullptr;\nbool quickLayout = digitPressed != -1 && (activeDrag || (!dragging && win && ctrl && alt));\nif (quickLayout) { PostQuickLayoutKey(digitPressed); }
edge_cases: Clear or reject the path when a window is destroyed and the snapper is null.
Preserve numpad digit handling and existing quick-layout trace events.
Do not consume ordinary digits outside a live drag.
tests: Preserve the destroy-mid-drag number typing regression.

verify: Build FancyZonesLib with tools\build\build.ps1 -Platform x64 -Configuration Release -Project src\modules\fancyzones\FancyZonesLib\FancyZonesLib.vcxproj.
Build and run the existing FancyZones native tests with vstest.console.exe after locating the produced test DLL.
Enable two personal layouts, drag a window, press Shift+2, and confirm layout 2 is active without ending the drag.
Destroy or abort a drag, focus Notepad, and confirm number keys type normally.
risks: A stale active-drag signal could capture digits; requiring the live snapper and clearing it on every move-size exit limits that risk.
UI tests need an interactive desktop and clean FancyZones settings.
alternatives: Keeping Win+Ctrl+Alt during drag preserves the regression but breaks existing behavior.
Adding a new setting increases surface area and does not fix the accidental guard.

mirror.fork_title: [Issue 50149] FancyZones quick layout switching during drag

adversary.notes: The live snapper guard retains the stale-state protection.

comment.body: Approve the fork-side FancyZones design for Issue 50149 and allow the implementation workflow to begin.
